author: Brett Mills
title: Perry County reeling from severe floods, recovery efforts underway - NewsBreak
text:
By Brett Mills ,
6 hours ago
CROOKSVILLE, Ohio ( WCMH ) — Major flooding that reached levels as high as eight feet in parts of Crooksville has now subsided, but the debris and damage remain.
Residents like IGA — a Crooksville grocery store — co-manager Julie Pletcher are still in utter shock at the damage.
“I’ve been here for 51 years. I’ve seen it once or twice, but not as bad as this store was yesterday,” Pletcher said. “I mean, everybody here, Crooksville is just devastated.”
Brian Paul, another resident, said the first floor of his home was filled with two feet of water Tuesday.
“I lost everything, all my tools, I built dirt because of course, everything’s ruined, so there’s no point in me even trying at this point,” Paul said. “The main thing is to get the house fixed and start back over.”
Ohio national guard members have also been activated to help the people in Crooksville and neighboring Roseville.
“I hope we get the help that we need so everyone can get back on their feet.”
Officials said they completed 35 water rescues on one street alone Tuesday. Pletcher spent all morning getting the flood water out of the store, and was forced to throw out all of their meat as Crooksville still waits for power to be restored.
“Hopefully we get it back up and running and we can get this store opened up and help people out in this community to get groceries to them and stuff,” Pletcher said.
